headline: Rising yields temper AI-driven optimism as markets await payrolls
body: Equity futures opened October mixed rather than directional: Nasdaq-100 contracts added roughly half a percent and S&P 500 futures ticked higher after Micron's fiscal Q4 beat reinforced the AI-memory demand story, while Dow futures slipped as rate-sensitive industrials and financials lagged. The more consequential story is in the bond market — the 10-year Treasury yield has pushed to its highest level since 2002, driven by stickier, energy-linked inflation readings that have pushed the Fed's expected path from cuts toward a possible hike at the October 28 meeting. Attention now shifts to Friday's nonfarm payrolls report, with consensus near 90,000 jobs and unemployment holding around 4.1%; a hotter-than-expected print would likely pressure yields, and equities, further.

Retail chatter looks concentrated rather than broad-based: Reddit's trading boards are clustering around the AI-memory trade, with Micron, SK Hynix and Sandisk drawing heavy bullish comment volume on the view that tight supply and surging AI storage demand extend well beyond Micron's own earnings beat. Sentiment on mega-cap names is more split — Nvidia and Amazon drew plenty of engagement but no clear directional consensus, while chatter pointed to souring sentiment on Microsoft alongside quickly building interest in Uber. With no government-shutdown overhang clouding the picture (a funding bill passed in September runs through mid-December), the dominant mood looks like selective, narrative-driven enthusiasm in AI-adjacent pockets set against a broader market still digesting the jump in long-term yields.
